newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity closes mixed in lackluster trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity closes mixed in lackluster trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled mixed after a day of lackluster trade, with many players in New York for a meeting with the exchange, market sources said Monday.
"A lot of traders were away from their jobs for the meeting," said one utility trade source.
"The market has just been trading sideways and will probably stay there," he added.
But another dealer said pointed to more activity in forward-month contracts, particularly at Palo Verde (PV), as an encouraging sign for the market.
Forward cash prices were also described as lifeless on Monday, although next-day prices gained ground amid cooler-than-expected short-term weather forecasts.
Temperatures in the Pacific Northwest were expected to drop to below normal later in the week and to average below to much below normal over the next six to 10 days.

The Southwest was forecast to see above normal temperatures through Friday, while the six to 10 day forecast was for below normal temperatures across western sections and normal to above normal across eastern sections.
In the Southwest, outages continued at a 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3 nuclear unit and a 750 MW Navajo coal-fired unit.
The 1,070 MW San Onofre nuclear unit in California is expected to restart Friday after a refueling outage that began Nov 30 was extended for additional repair work.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear unit in Washington was expected to ramp down Wednesday night for an extended refueling outage due to last until early July.
The April California-Oregon border (COB) contract settled up 10 cents at $9.40 per megawatt hour (MWh), while May was up 15 cents at $9.55.
June and July COB were both up 10 cents at $10.35 and $13.35, respectivley.
April PV settled unchanged at $13.15, while May was down 5 cents at $13.65.
The June PV contract closed 5 cents lower at $14.95 and July closed 10 cents lower at $19.35.
